Audit: RAIS formal employment aggregate

Published

October 7, 2026

Source: own BigQuery extraction from Base dos Dados RAIS (basedosdados.br_me_rais.microdados_vinculos, update 2025-08-26); Query 2 output, table social_employment_1.export_table_v4 (created 2025-11-25), exported 2026-10-06 (_scripts/sql/2026-10-06-export-table-v4.sql). Raw file: _data/raw/rais/export_table_v4.csv. Pipeline script: _scripts/02-social-rais.R. Interim output: _data/interim/rais_employment_1999_2024.rds. The brief’s questions on CBO codes around the agricultural cutoff and on public administration need the vínculo-level table and belong to the RAIS track (rebuild/upstream-reform-rais.md), not to this aggregate.

Code 
rais_raw <- read_csv("_data/raw/rais/export_table_v4.csv",
                     col_types = cols(geocode = col_character(), .default = col_integer()))
rais <- read_rds("_data/interim/rais_employment_1999_2024.rds")
biome_amz <- read_delim("_data/raw/ibge/ibge_bioma.csv", delim = ";",
                        col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
                        locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(str_detect(Geocódigo, "^[0-9]{7}$"), `Bioma predominante` == "Amazônia")

Q1. What does the export contain, and how is it distributed?

What is checked: rows, years, municipalities per year, the wage-code and agricultural splits, and the national totals by year.

Code 
tibble(rows = nrow(rais_raw), years = paste(range(rais_raw$year), collapse = "-"),
       municipalities = n_distinct(rais_raw$geocode),
       duplicate_keys = anyDuplicated(rais_raw[, c("year", "geocode", "workers_agricultural",
                                                   "wage_code")]),
       zero_counts = sum(rais_raw$workers_total == 0))
# A tibble: 1 × 5
    rows years     municipalities duplicate_keys zero_counts
   <int> <chr>              <int>          <int>       <int>
1 174062 1999-2024            808              0           0
Code 
rais_raw %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(municipalities = n_distinct(geocode), workers_millions = sum(workers_total) / 1e6,
            agri_share = sum(workers_total[workers_agricultural == 1]) / sum(workers_total),
            low_share = sum(workers_total[wage_code == 1]) / sum(workers_total),
            high_share = sum(workers_total[wage_code >= 5]) / sum(workers_total)) %>%
  print(n = 26)

rais_raw %>% count(wage_code, wt = workers_total, name = "workers") %>%
  mutate(share = workers / sum(workers))
# A tibble: 6 × 3
  wage_code  workers  share
      <int>    <int>  <dbl>
1         1 20500828 0.232

4         4  5890516 0.0666
5         5  3343867 0.0378
6         6  7515868 0.0850

Finding. The export holds 174,062 rows for 808 municipalities of the nine Legal Amazon states, 1999-2024, with no zero counts and no duplicate keys. Formal employment grows from 1.6 million bonds in 1999 to over 4 million from 2013; the agricultural (CBO group 6) share stays around 4-5 percent after 2003, while the share in the lowest bracket falls from 48 percent to under 15 percent. This is the aggregate the lost _data/data_employment_rais held, re-materialised from the surviving BigQuery table. Decision. none required (D-2026-10-05-d governs the brackets). Assertion. 02-social-rais.R, raw-state block (row count, years, municipalities, codes, no duplicates).

Q2. Which municipality-years have no RAIS rows?

What is checked: the 808 × 26 grid against the rows present, and the missing municipality-years of the Amazon-biome sample in 2000-2020, which the panel carries as NA employment.

missing <- grid %>% anti_join(rais, by = c("geocode", "year"))

Code 
missing %>% filter(geocode %in% biome_amz$Geocódigo, year %in% 2000:2020) %>% nrow()
[1] 64

Finding. The gaps concentrate in the early years and in municipalities installed after 2000 (which have no bonds before installation) and in a few small municipalities with no active bond in a year. Within the Amazon-biome sample and the 2000-2020 window, 64 municipality-years are absent: 13 are Mojuí dos Campos before 2013 (dropped downstream), and the remaining 51 are the rows the recovered panel shows as NA in every emp_* column (phase 1 check). The script does not fill them: a missing municipality-year is not a zero. Decision. none required; task 1.8 (NA versus zero) documents the rule. Assertion. none in script 02 (the grid is completed in script 04).

Q3. Where do the agricultural wage-group counts and the shares turn NA?

What is checked: the inherited replace_na() defect, which filled the all-worker wage-group counts with 0 but left the agricultural ones NA where a municipality-year has no bond at all in that wage group, and the 0 / 0 shares (task 1.8).

Code 
rais %>%
  summarise(across(c(workers_low, workers_mid, workers_high), ~ sum(is.na(.x)),
                   .names = "na_{.col}"),
            across(c(workers_agri_low, workers_agri_mid, workers_agri_high), ~ sum(is.na(.x)),
                   .names = "na_{.col}"),
            zero_workers_agric = sum(workers_agric == 0))
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  na_workers_low na_workers_mid na_workers_high na_workers_agri_low na_workers_agri_mid na_workers_agri_high
           <int>          <int>           <int>               <int>               <int>                <int>
1              0              0               0                 107                 157                 2451
# ℹ 1 more variable: zero_workers_agric <int>
Code

  summarise(across(starts_with("emp_share_agri_"), ~ sum(is.na(.x)), .names = "na_{.col}"),
            rows = n())
# A tibble: 1 × 5
  na_emp_share_agri_low_workers na_emp_share_agri_mid_wo…¹ na_emp_share_agri_hi…² na_emp_share_agri_wo…³  rows
                          <int>                      <int>                  <int>                  <int> <int>
1                          2721                       2769                   4240                      0 20868
# ℹ abbreviated names: ¹​na_emp_share_agri_mid_workers, ²​na_emp_share_agri_high_workers,
#   ³​na_emp_share_agri_workers
Code 
rais %>%
  mutate(agri_zero = workers_agric == 0, high_na = is.na(workers_agri_high)) %>%
  count(agri_zero, high_na)
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  agri_zero high_na     n
  <lgl>     <lgl>   <int>
1 FALSE     FALSE   16628
2 FALSE     TRUE     1522
3 TRUE      FALSE    1789
4 TRUE      TRUE      929

Finding. The all-worker counts are never NA, while the agricultural counts are NA wherever the municipality-year has no bond in that bracket at all (most often the high bracket of small municipalities); the lost script’s replace_na() named the wrong columns. The agricultural shares are NA both there and where no agricultural bond exists (0 / 0). The pipeline reproduces the pattern and stores 0 / 0 as NA rather than NaN. Decision. open (task 1.8: keep NA, add the denominator count so that “no agricultural employment” can be told from “missing”; the replace_na() defect is fixed in the same step). Assertion. 02-social-rais.R, output block (shares within 0-1 or NA; the three all-worker shares sum to one).

Q4. How are the rates and shares distributed?

What is checked: quantiles by year of the PIA rates and the wage shares, and the municipality-years with a rate above one.

Code 
rais %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2024)) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(across(c(emp_pia_rate_total, emp_share_low_workers, emp_share_agri_workers),
                   list(p10 = ~ quantile(.x, .1, na.rm = TRUE), p50 = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        p90 = ~ quantile(.x, .9, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-year) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = year, values_from = value)

Code 
rais %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, emp_pia_rate_total, group = geocode)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.08) + theme_minimal()

Finding. The median municipality has formal employment near 3 percent of its working-age population in 2000 and about 10 percent by the mid-2010s; the median low-wage share of bonds falls from 75 to 13 percent. Three municipality-years exceed a rate of one (5107800 in 2000-2001, 1720259 in 2007), where the bonds counted outnumber the interpolated PIA; kept as inherited. Decision. none required. Assertion. 02-social-rais.R, output block (counts add up; shares within 0-1).
